title: Al-Fil: the elephant
hookLine: the army of the elephant and the birds with stones (Surah 105)

cards: A desert town with no walls and no army. Coming up the road from the south is a real army, and with it an elephant, maybe more than one, marching toward the one building the town is known for.
The townspeople do the only thing they can. They leave, and they go up into the hills to watch. This happened, according to Muslim tradition, in the year the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ was born.

teach.b: Surah one hundred five opens, in Pickthall's translation: Hast thou not seen how thy Lord dealt with the owners of the Elephant? The Qur'an tells it in five lines and names no one.
The historians and commentators fill in the names.

The army came from Yemen, led by a ruler named Abraha who, the story goes, had built a great church and wanted the Arabs to make pilgrimage there instead of to the Ka'bah. So he marched to destroy it.

The early biography of the Prophet keeps a well-known scene. Abraha's men seized camels belonging to Abd al-Muttalib, the Prophet's grandfather and a leader of Mecca. He went to Abraha and asked for his camels back.
Abraha was surprised: I've come to destroy your holy House, and you ask about camels?

teach.h: I AM THE LORD OF THE CAMELS.
teach.b: And Abd al-Muttalib is remembered as saying: I am the lord of the camels. The House has its own Lord, who will protect it. Then the surah tells what happened.

teach.h: BIRDS IN FLOCKS, STONES OF CLAY.
teach.b: Allah sent birds in flocks, ababil, pelting the army with stones of baked clay, and left them like chewed-up straw.

Tradition says the Arabs counted years from it, the Year of the Elephant, and places the Prophet's birth in that year, around five hundred seventy. So the surah reminds Quraysh of something their own elders saw.
They didn't defend the House. They couldn't. They went up into the hills.

how: Surah al-Fil is recited in the prayers, and the story of Abraha and the Year of the Elephant is taught as part of the Prophet's biography, since tradition places his birth in that year.

o: the stones of baked clay that fell on them
the elephant that marched with Abraha's army
the flocks of birds that pelted the army

games.q: who's who in the story — tap the pairs.

s: the Qur'an names Abraha in the surah
the surah names no one; the names come from the historians and commentators.
the people of Mecca fought off the army
they left the town and watched from the hills. the House was defended without them.
tradition says the Arabs counted years from this event
the Year of the Elephant, placed around 570 by tradition.

games.q: you're Abd al-Muttalib. the invader who has come to destroy the Ka'bah has seized your camels. you go to see him. what do you ask for?
games.why: he asked for his camels, and said: I am the lord of the camels; the House has its own Lord, who will protect it.

practice: Remember a time you were protected, when something could have gone badly and didn't: a near miss on the road, a diagnosis that came back clear, someone who stepped in for you.
Notice how little of it you controlled, and let yourself feel the relief again. If you pray, you can say alhamdulillah for it, as if it happened today.

wordCard.voice: Al-Fil. The elephant, the name of Surah one hundred five, about the army that marched on the Ka'bah. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: the elephant; the name of Surah 105.

carryVoice: Your line: the house was defended. Abd al-Muttalib asked only for his camels. Day one hundred sixty-nine, done.
